required_fixes: Re-pin candidate GGUF digests to the byte-level sha256 of the served body (verified by full download) and re-freeze, preserving candidate identities (model, quant, chat_format, URL) and correcting only the digest/bytes binding; OR vendor exact GGUF bytes in an immutable artifact store keyed by byte sha256; OR at DESIGN time compute candidate digests from downloaded bytes rather than HF server metadata (etag/xetHash).

Add a byte-verification step to the freeze_eligibility.freeze_artifacts_bound check for any experiment pinning remote GGUFs: the freeze must verify sha256 against downloaded body bytes, not server metadata (etag/xetHash/lfs.oid), and the provenance must record which hash source was used.
validity_findings: The frozen capability ladder (primary gating component) was never executed: both candidates failed at frozen step 3a (byte-level digest verification) because the pinned sha256 values equal the HF tree-API xetHash / CDN etag, while the served body bytes hash to the tree-API lfs.oid. Three independent download routes reproduced identical body hashes and byte counts, confirming the served content is stable and authentic, and the frozen byte-level identity is unsatisfiable against it.

The spec.json note 'sha256 equals the HF LFS OID (CDN etag)' conflated two distinct HF metadata fields (xetHash/etag vs lfs.oid). The freeze_eligibility.freeze_artifacts_bound check (status PASS) appears to have been satisfied via server metadata inspection rather than byte download, allowing a metadata/body mismatch to silently pass freeze.

No model was loaded and no capability measurement was taken for either candidate (UNMEASURED_LOAD_FAILED, fail-closed per frozen rule 3a). The OUTCOME=MEASUREMENT_INVALID and B3_STATUS=UNRESOLVED are the correct frozen decision-rule mappings for zero COMPLETE cells (rule 4).

The PREFLIGHT controls (PC-ORACLE-EPISODE 5/5, NC-NO-MODEL-ACTION 0/0, B-RANDOM-ACTION parseable 1.0 / success 0.2) passed deterministically through the real frozen scorer against the served page, and raw/controls.json is byte-identical to the audited parent's (sha256 b0120e61...). The measurement substrate (scorer, browser, task page, parsing) is live and verified.

The endpoint census (12 providers, non-gating) and external-comparator readiness table (3 entries, all CANDIDATE_NOT_EVIDENCE) were executed correctly and recorded as observations; they do not override the frozen OUTCOME.

The per-candidate config overlays are confined to the predeclared three keys (prompts.system, sampling.chat_format, candidate_models_frozen) with no leakage; materialized configs' sha256s are recorded and verified.

This is a substrate/provisioning failure (unobtainable frozen GGUF byte identity), not a scientific negative. The producer correctly encodes it as MEASUREMENT_INVALID and does not promote, weaken, or falsify C-LLM-INHERIT.

claim_ceiling: The capability question (whether M-14B-QWEN or M-8B-LLAMA clears the minimal multi-step Web-agent bar under the frozen protocol) remains entirely unmeasured. No claim advancement, weakening, or falsification of C-LLM-INHERIT is justified by this transaction. The inherited Codex effective event for C-LLM-INHERIT remains the parent EXP-INTEL-38164607941 FALSIFIES (bounded to the tested 3B–8B Qwen class under goal/schema prompt). The operational finding established is a freeze-process failure mode: HF GGUF pins from server metadata (xetHash/etag) can differ from served-body sha256 (lfs.oid) while byte counts match, silently defeating byte-identity gates.
